text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Simon Wiesenthal Centre called for a boycott of the events sponsored by the Lithuanian government to mark the 200th anniversary of the demise of the Gaon of Vilnius, scheduled in September.
The centre said that it would be inappropriate for Israeli and American Jewish groups to take part in the events because of Lithuania's failure to try alleged war criminals on its soil.
- The government said it will amend the criminal code in September to allow those charged with genocide to be tried regardless of the state of their health.
- Homeland Union MP Raimonas Rajackas, 60, died at home on Monday after a long illness.
- Lithuanian Savings Bank posted 10.1 million litas audited losses for the first half of the year.
- Lithuanian national Jolanta Babrauskiene was detained in Copenhagen airport for allegedly attempting to smuggle four kilograms of cocaine from Athens. She was using a forged Dutch passport.
- The director of the state security department Jurgis Jurgelis said that the ultra-radical groups in Lithuania are small and insignificant.
- The government plans to sell its 9.9 percent stake in pharmaceutical producer Sanitas in September.
- Experts expect that the grain harvest in Lithuania will be around 2.7 billion tonnes this year.
